provenance.instrument: Schuylkill Township Zoning Ordinance of 1955, as amended (Chapter 370 Zoning, amended in its entirety 3-19-1997), as published on eCode360
provenance.status_detail: eCode360 SC2895, Township of Schuylkill, Chester County (370-7 'Board of Supervisors': 'The governing or legislative body of Schuylkill Township, Chester County, Pennsylvania'). District use lists and lot, yard and height figures are text in Articles III to XVII and XXIX. Attachments 1 and 2 are only summary tables of uses and bulk figures. Floodplain rules are in Article XI of the zoning chapter and in Chapter 186. New Laws: none
provenance.code_current_through_note: eCode360 table of contents: 'Includes legislation through 08-10-2026.' New Laws: none
checks: Accessory dwelling unit: 'A dwelling unit on the same lot with and of a nature customarily incidental and subordinate to the principal use or structure' (370-7, Ord. No. 2019-05). The code allows one only in a conservation subdivision under Option 2, country properties, of the Conservation Overlay District, on a conservancy lot of 10 or more acres (370-229C)

The Conservation Overlay District lies over FR and R-1. It applies in FR to tracts of seven acres of developable area or more with more than three dwelling units, and in R-1 to tracts of five acres or more with more than five units (370-226C). On smaller tracts compliance with the overlay is optional but not required, so an owner may elect it there (370-16B(2)(a), 370-20C(2)(a)). Option 2 allows one dwelling unit per 10 acres of gross tract area, plus the ADUs (370-229A, D(3))

ADU standards: it harmonizes with the look of the house. It sits inside the house or in existing or new outbuildings such as barns, stables, carriage houses, garages and springhouses. At most 1,200 sq ft of gross floor area in a new outbuilding or an addition. In an existing historic dwelling or structure it may be larger, up to 50% of the house. It meets the setbacks of the underlying FR or R-1 district, except a historic structure on the Historic Properties Map reused as an ADU (370-229C(1) to (5))

Option 2 lots: at least 60,000 sq ft, 140 ft wide, 50 ft of street frontage, front yard 100 ft, rear 50 ft, side 20 ft, accessory buildings 10 ft, height 35 ft. Impervious cover falls from 50% on lots under 10,000 sq ft to 20% at 20,000 to 43,560 sq ft, then by 1.5% an acre, with at most 20,000 sq ft. New dwelling units stand 100 ft from external road rights-of-way, 50 ft from other tract lines, 100 ft from cropland or pasture and 300 ft from livestock buildings, and 150 ft from active recreation areas (370-230A to C)

Accessory buildings: over 150 sq ft they meet the district height and yards. All accessory structures are limited to 20 ft in height and a footprint of 750 sq ft. In R-1 and R-2 an accessory building may be erected in the rear yard (370-132E, J, K, 370-22, 370-27)

Floodplain: the F Flood Hazard and Wetlands District covers land within 50 ft of the banks of perennial streams and ponds of an acre or more, and the 100-year floodplain. Only listed uses are allowed there and accessory structures are prohibited. No structure may stand within 50 ft of the district's boundary, so none within 100 ft of such a bank. Any new structure is prohibited in the floodway, and any demolition in the district is a conditional use (370-71A, 370-73A(4), D(7), G, 370-74E). Chapter 186 prohibits new construction and substantial improvements in the identified floodplain unless a variance is granted, and bars new construction within 50 ft landward of the top of bank there, plus a 50 ft no-structure setback beyond the land the base flood reaches (186-23, 186-22D). Chapter 186 variances are granted by the Board of Supervisors (186-35)

Riparian buffer: the inner buffer runs at least 50 ft from the top of each streambank, farther where steep slopes or the FEMA floodplain reach beyond it, and no earth disturbance is allowed there. The outer buffer adds 50 ft, of which at most 10% may be disturbed. No buildings on steep slopes over 15% (370-7, 370-223C, D). Wetlands get a 50 ft setback and may not be filled or built upon without state and federal permits (370-75, 370-223F(3))

Two units otherwise: APO I lists two-family dwellings in a development by special exception (370-31A(2)), and APO I and APO II list the conversion of a single-family dwelling by special exception under 370-149 (two or more units, each with at least 800 sq ft of habitable floor area). NC and C allow dwelling units above a ground-floor business by special exception (370-78B, 370-86G(11)). A Class I or II historic property may add listed uses by conditional use, including multifamily dwellings in FR and R-1 (370-58)
Parking: two all-weather spaces per dwelling (370-181A)

Variances: the Zoning Hearing Board on the findings of 370-209. No bar on a use variance was found. A lot held in single and separate ownership at the chapter's effective date that is below the minimum area or width may be built on, with a special exception where the yards cannot be met (370-187)

Uses not listed: 370-148 reaches only a use not listed as permitted by right, special exception or conditional use in any district. The ADU is listed in the Conservation Overlay District, so 370-148 does not reach it

Two-family conversion lot size: under 370-149C the lot must hold the district minimum times the number of families. In APO I the residential minimum is 5 acres of developable area (370-33B), so about 10 acres for two units

term.note: 'A dwelling unit on the same lot with and of a nature customarily incidental and subordinate to the principal use or structure.' The only rule for one is in the Conservation Overlay District

status.note: Option 2, country properties, is permitted by right, with 'the opportunity for accessory dwelling units on the lots'. One ADU is permitted on a conservancy lot of 10 or more acres

scope_districts.note: The Conservation Overlay District is an overlay on FR and R-1

status_outside.note: The other districts' use lists name no ADU and end 'and no other'

fallback_path.note: Zoning Hearing Board on the findings of 370-209A(1) to (5). No bar on a use variance was found

value.name: Conversion of a single-family dwelling into two or more units (APO I, APO II)
value.conditions: A single-family detached dwelling that existed before the chapter took effect may be converted into a two-family or multifamily dwelling. The lot area must be at least the district minimum times the number of families, each dwelling needs at least 800 sq ft of habitable floor area, and there may be no external alteration except for safety. Parking per 370-181

requires.condition: The house existed before the effective date of the chapter

value.note: A house divided into units, not a unit added to it. APO I and APO II need public water and sewer for land development (370-36, 370-43). The lot must hold the district minimum times the number of families (370-149C). In APO I that is 5 acres of developable area per family under 370-33B, so about 10 acres for two units. The APO II minimum was not read

value.name: Two-family dwellings in a development (APO I)
value.conditions: Multifamily housing, townhouses, semidetached, quadraplex and two-family dwellings under 370-143. At least 5 acres of developable area, buildings on individual lots under Chapter 320, net density of at most five units per acre of developable area, front yard 40 ft, rear 30 ft, side yards 10 ft each and 25 ft together for two-family dwellings, and public water and sewer
value.note: A new development, not a unit added to a house. 370-143 was not read

building_types.note: The Conservation Overlay District permits single-family detached dwellings

districts_read_no_listing.note: None of these use lists names an accessory dwelling unit

districts_in_doubt.note: R-2 permits 'Any use permitted in Article IV, 370-20', which includes single-family dwellings in Option 2 conservation subdivisions, but 370-226C makes the Conservation Overlay District an overlay on FR and R-1 only

notes_by_district.R-2: R-2 permits 'Any use permitted in Article IV, 370-20', which includes single-family dwellings in Option 2 conservation subdivisions, but 370-226C makes the Conservation Overlay District an overlay on FR and R-1 only
notes_by_district.APO I: APO I permits 'Any use permitted as a use by right in the R-2 Residential District', and R-2 takes the R-1 uses, which include Option 2 conservation subdivisions. But 370-226C makes the Conservation Overlay District an overlay on FR and R-1 only

value.condition: An ADU is allowed only on a conservancy lot in a conservation subdivision of the Conservation Overlay District. The overlay applies in FR to tracts of seven acres of developable area or more and in R-1 to tracts of five acres or more, and a smaller tract may elect it. A conventional lot, or a lot in an Option 1 subdivision alone, does not qualify. A conservancy lot holds part of the required conservation land, and Option 2 alone requires none, so in practice the ADU comes with Option 2 combined with an option that requires conservation land, as 370-229B(3) and 370-233A(4) read.

The ADU belongs to Option 2, country properties. 370-226B(2), Table 370-229A, Tables 370-230A to D and 370-229C all tie country properties and ADUs to Option 2, so the weight of the text is Option 2. A lot in an Option 3 estate lot subdivision qualifies only on the other reading.

disputed_by.note: The definition says a conservancy lot is 'created under Option 3 of the Conservation Overlay District', and 370-229B(3) speaks of 'Option 3, country properties'. Read so, a conservancy lot in an Option 3 subdivision may also hold an ADU

value.condition: 'one ADU is permitted on a conservancy lot of 10 or more acres'. A conservancy lot is privately owned, holds an existing dwelling, agricultural structure or historic structure, and is part of the required conservation land under a conservation easement.

A lot in a conservation subdivision follows Article XXIX, not the FR or R-1 lot figures (370-16B, 370-20C). Option 2 lot figures: at least 60,000 sq ft, 140 ft wide, front yard 100 ft, rear 50 ft, side 20 ft, accessory buildings 10 ft, height 35 ft. Impervious cover on a lot over one acre is 20% less 1.5% for each added acre, and at most 20,000 sq ft. Article XXIX gives no building coverage figure. New dwelling units stand 100 ft from external road rights-of-way, 50 ft from other tract lines, 100 ft from cropland or pasture, 300 ft from livestock buildings and 150 ft from active recreation areas. The ADU must meet 'all the setback standards in the applicable underlying FR or R-1 Zoning District', so the district yards are shown, and whether the Option 2 yards govern instead is not settled.
The ADU must harmonize with the appearance of the principal dwelling and is in addition to the tract's dwelling unit limit.

In the F Flood Hazard and Wetlands District only the listed uses are allowed, 'all uses not allowed as permitted uses or authorized by grant of variance or by special exception shall be prohibited', and accessory structures are prohibited. Any new structure is prohibited in the floodway.
overlays: F Flood Hazard and Wetlands District

value.condition: In the F Flood Hazard and Wetlands District 'Any modification, alteration, reconstruction, removal, replacement or improvement of any kind to an existing structure shall constitute a substantial improvement' and must fully comply, elevated or floodproofed. Chapter 186 counts only work of 50% or more of the market value, so the zoning chapter's rule is the stricter one.
overlays: F Flood Hazard and Wetlands District

value.condition: The F Flood Hazard and Wetlands District reaches at least 50 ft from the banks of perennial streams and of ponds of an acre or more, and 'no structure shall be placed less than 50 feet from the boundary of any Flood Hazard and Wetlands District'. So no new structure within 100 ft of such a bank, and farther where the 100-year floodplain reaches. Where no FEMA study maps the stream, any watercourse under Chapter 105 counts.

Within any identified floodplain area 'any new construction or substantial improvements shall be prohibited', and no new construction or development may stand within 50 ft landward of the top of bank of any watercourse, extended to the land the base flood reaches, with a further 50 ft no-structure setback. A variance under Chapter 186, which the Board of Supervisors grants, and Article XI of the zoning chapter may allow new construction, with the lowest floor at or above the regulatory flood elevation.

The inner riparian buffer runs at least 50 ft from the top of each streambank, farther where steep slopes or the FEMA 100-year floodplain extend beyond it, and 'No woodland disturbance or other earth disturbance shall be permitted' there beyond trails, hazard removal and conservation work.

The outer riparian buffer adds 50 ft beyond the inner buffer and at most 10% of it may be disturbed. 'There shall be no erection of buildings or streets on steep slopes' (slopes over 15%), and woodland disturbance on a lot is capped at 25%.

There is a setback of 50 ft from the border of any wetlands. Wetlands may not be regraded, filled, drained, built upon or otherwise disturbed except with state and federal permits, and at most 10% of the wetland buffer may be disturbed.

On a property with a Class I historic resource, a new principal or accessory structure needs a historic resource impact study reviewed by the Historical Commission, and exterior changes to a Class I or II resource need the Commission's review before a building permit.

types_allowed.note: 'located within the principal dwelling unit or in existing or new outbuildings (such as barns, stables, carriage houses, garages and springhouses)'. 370-229C(3) also names 'an addition to a principal dwelling'

max_sqft_by_form.note: 'The gross floor area of the ADU shall not exceed 1,200 square feet when located in new outbuildings or in an addition to a principal dwelling.' No figure is given for a unit inside the house or in an existing outbuilding. The next sentence lets a unit in an existing historic building 'exceed the floor area limit', which may mean the 1,200 sq ft applies to every other form, so the size of a unit in the house or in an existing non-historic building is not settled

value.what: a historic structure on the Schuylkill Township Historic Properties Map reused as an ADU

exempt_building.note: Exempt from the district setbacks. An ADU in an existing historic dwelling or structure may exceed 1,200 sq ft, up to 50% of the gross floor area of the house

max_adus.note: 'one ADU is permitted on a conservancy lot of 10 or more acres'

max_height_ft.note: 'All accessory structures as identified in this chapter shall be limited to a height of 20 feet.' Read for a unit in an outbuilding. 370-132E(3) sends a building over 150 sq ft to the district height (35 ft), so the lower figure is the safe reading

district_yards_bind_accessory.note: 'An accessory building or structure which exceeds 150 square feet shall meet the height and yard regulations of the district in which it is located.' 370-229C(4) also ties the ADU to the district setbacks

accessory_rear_yard_only.note: 'An accessory use building or other structure may be erected in the rear yard in accordance with Article XIX, 370-132'

value.where: Every accessory building or structure is limited to a footprint of 750 sq ft. A unit in a new outbuilding over that footprint would need a second story or relief.

spaces_required.note: 'Two all-weather parking spaces per dwelling'. An ADU is a dwelling unit, so it is read to need its own two

total_on_site.note: Two for the house and two for the ADU

reading.value: 'Two all-weather parking spaces per dwelling' may be read per building, so a unit in the house or attached to it may need no added spaces, and two in all

min_lot_sqft.note: Residential use. At least 43,560 sq ft of developable area per lot. Option 2 conservation lots follow 370-230A instead

setback_side_ft.note: Side yard abutting a street 100 ft

max_building_coverage.note: Building coverage is measured against the developable area of the lot (370-7). A lot in a conservation subdivision follows Article XXIX instead

max_impervious_coverage.note: 'Maximum lot coverage 20%'. Lot coverage is the share of the developable area 'covered by any and all impervious materials'. A lot in a conservation subdivision follows 370-230B instead

min_lot_replaced_in_planned_development.note: A lot in a conservation subdivision complies with Article XXIX, whose Option 2 lots are at least 60,000 sq ft

min_lot_sqft.note: With public sewer and water. Option 2 conservation lots follow 370-230B to D instead

setback_side_ft.note: Side yard abutting a street 50 ft

max_building_coverage.note: Building coverage is measured against the developable area of the lot (370-7). A lot in a conservation subdivision follows Article XXIX instead

max_impervious_coverage.note: 'Maximum lot coverage', which counts impervious materials on the developable area of the lot (370-7). A lot in a conservation subdivision follows 370-230B instead

value.when: Public sewer is available, no public water

utility_rows.note: Developable area per lot 43,560 sq ft in both rows. Building coverage 10% and lot coverage 25% in every row

min_lot_replaced_in_planned_development.note: A lot in a conservation subdivision complies with Article XXIX, whose Option 2 lots are at least 60,000 sq ft

setback_side_ft.note: Side yard abutting a street 40 ft

value.when: Public sewer is available, no public water
